grh_096efa17bbbb5f9b9dc9.title: Love On A Diet
paragraphs: Dorothy Corbett breaks down after her daughter Margo, looking at an old photograph, innocently remarks that Dorothy used to be pretty. Dr. Christian discovers that years with domineering, jealous husband Dave have stripped Dorothy of nearly every pleasure and sign of individuality: she no longer goes out, dresses attractively or receives the affection she once knew. Treating the problem as emotional starvation rather than an ordinary illness, he and Margo restore Dorothy's hair, clothes and confidence and arrange harmless masculine attention from Arnold Darrow, who is actually Margo's fiancé. Dave returns unexpectedly, sees his transformed wife with Arnold and assumes an affair, even threatening divorce and blaming Dr. Christian. The doctor forces Dave to confront the truth that his possessiveness has nearly destroyed Dorothy. When Margo reveals Arnold belongs to her, Dorothy's collapse finally breaks through Dave's anger. He calls his wife by the old pet name 'Dolly' and resumes the tenderness he abandoned years earlier, giving her a reason to want life again.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on December 27, 1939. It is listed as episode 60 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt, Rosemary De Camp, Gloria Holden, Charles Webster, and Helen Claire. Other credited names include Andre Baruch as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 29 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_09070191c790705984cf.title: Carousel
paragraphs: Carnival barker Billy Bigelow falls in love with Julie Jordan and marries her, but fear about providing for their expected child draws him into a robbery that ends in his death. From the outskirts of heaven Billy is allowed one day back on earth, where he tries clumsily to help his troubled teenage daughter Louise and leaves her a star. grh_097b537d3ccdc723c0c5.title: Sheriff Billy
paragraphs: New young sheriff Billy Riddle astonishes Dawson by arresting notorious gunman Ben Reed without even drawing. Britt later learns why Reed surrendered so quietly: before becoming an outlaw he was Blake Riddle, Billy's estranged father, who abandoned his old identity after his wife left with their son. Billy does not initially know the truth, but Reed cannot bring himself to fight the boy who has grown into the lawman confronting him. He allows Billy to deliver him to the marshal and, contrary to everyone's expectations, makes no attempt to escape.

grh_0974790084db51bd8c3a.title: No Escape
paragraphs: Condemned prisoner Rogan is obsessed with revenge against Mark Street, the man he says betrayed him and caused the death at the center of his case. He escapes death row through flooded sewers, murdering a fellow prisoner during the flight, only to learn that Street has already died. paragraphs: John’s marriage explodes when his hard-drinking wife Linda admits she married him for money, has emptied his bank account and intends to throw him out.
